methodology.selection: At each origin, use the candidate with lowest MAE on earlier forecasts whose annual outcomes were already available. A richer candidate needs at least five such forecasts and at least 5% lower MAE than the historical mean; otherwise use the historical mean.
methodology.range: Symmetric range from the finite-sample-adjusted 80th percentile of earlier absolute forecast errors. Historical coverage is measured separately; temporal dependence and data revisions prevent a guaranteed 80% probability interpretation.
methodology.coverageInterval: The Wilson interval is a descriptive small-sample binomial summary of observed coverage. Annual errors may be dependent, so it is not a validated interval for future coverage.
methodology.availability: Latest annual prior-year GDP is available by the spring; employment uses January through the displayed cutoff month. Historical folds use that same month cutoff. No training, selection or calibration outcome reaches the forecast-origin year.
limitations: These are model forecasts of real output, not causal estimates of an oil, gas or electricity price change.
Backtests use today’s revised historical data with simulated release timing, not the original published data vintages.
A short annual record gives limited evidence about forecast accuracy, especially during recessions, pandemics or structural change.
Prediction ranges describe earlier forecast errors. They do not guarantee future coverage and may miss new shocks.
Historical performance is reported for the complete selection procedure, including its simple-model fallback.
Employment has incomplete comparable monthly coverage in the territories, so no territorial GDP forecast is inferred.
Chained provincial GDP levels are not additive and these forecasts are not reconciled into a Canada total.
The next-year forecast uses current-year indicators; it does not know next-year employment, policies or commodity prices.

literature.title: A Three-Frequency Dynamic Factor Model for Nowcasting Canadian Provincial GDP Growth
literature.application: Timely provincial indicators and explicit data-release timing; this implementation is a small bridge model, not a replication of the full dynamic-factor model.

literature.title: Nowcasting Canadian GDP with Density Combinations
literature.application: Separate prediction accuracy from uncertainty calibration and distinguish revised-data exercises from actual real-time performance.

literature.title: The Accuracy of Short-Term Forecast Combinations
literature.application: Compare multiple model classes with simple benchmarks using only earlier predictive performance.

protocol.vintage: Revised historical data with simulated publication timing, not real-time vintages.
protocol.feature: Year-over-year change in January–July production totals. No missing-value imputation.
protocol.correction: Province-centred pooled ridge of prior incumbent forecast residuals on one energy-growth indicator. Subtract the province residual mean, cap at ±1 percentage point, then apply 50%.
protocol.selection: Use at least three earlier paired forecast years. Require at least 5% lower MAE and non-worse RMSE than the full incumbent. Choose the lowest-MAE eligible candidate; otherwise retain the incumbent.
